From their great stone palaces, the Medici direct a web of credit that reaches across Italy and beyond the Alps. A permanent house in Milan would place their clerks and reserves close to our court. In return for a charter and a subscription of two thousand ducats, the bank offers to bind its fortunes to our public credit, while keeping its existing accounts and obligations.

A local bank office. A sovereign with a Chartered Bank may pay for branches in foreign locations through normal construction, subject to the host’s relations and native building requirements. On completion the branch belongs to the Chartered Bank. New sovereign credit, deposits and investments require the bank’s completed branch in the sovereign’s current capital. Existing claims remain serviceable.
